text: There was a man in the land of Uz named Job. He was blameless and upright, a man who feared God and turned away from evil.
He had seven sons and three daughters.

His herds numbered seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, and five hundred donkeys, along with a great many servants, making him the greatest man among all the people of the east.
Job's sons used to take turns hosting feasts in their own houses, and they would send for their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

Whenever a round of feasting was finished, Job would send for his children and set them apart for purification, rising early the next morning to offer a burnt offering for each of them, thinking, 'Perhaps my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.' Job did this every time.
One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and the satan also came among them.
The LORD asked the satan, 'Where have you come from?' The satan answered, 'From roaming through the earth, going back and forth across it.'
The LORD said to him, 'Have you noticed my servant Job? There is no one like him on the earth — blameless, upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.'
The satan replied, 'Does Job fear God for nothing?
Haven't you built a wall around him and his household and everything he owns? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his herds have spread across the land.
But reach out and strike everything he has, and he will curse you to your face.'
The LORD told the satan, 'Very well — everything he has is now in your power, but do not lay a hand on the man himself.' So the satan left the LORD's presence.
One day while Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house,
a messenger came running to Job and said, 'The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them
when Sabean raiders swept in and carried them off, killing the servants with the sword. I alone escaped to bring you the news.'
While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived and said, 'Fire from God fell from the sky and burned up the sheep and the servants watching them. I alone escaped to bring you the news.'

While he was still speaking, yet another messenger arrived and said, 'Chaldeans formed three raiding parties, swept down on the camels, and carried them off, killing the servants with the sword. I alone escaped to bring you the news.'
While he was still speaking, one more messenger arrived and said, 'Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at the oldest brother's house
when suddenly a mighty wind swept in from the wilderness and struck all four corners of the house. It collapsed on the young people, and they died. I alone escaped to bring you the news.'
At this, Job got up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground and worshiped,
saying, 'Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; may the name of the LORD be praised.'
In all this, Job did not sin or charge God with wrongdoing.
